purpose-and-scope.text: This draft specifies registry operations, authorization and custody. It does not select an implementation language or application schema.

entities-and-terminology.text: Registry keys track Active or Over. The representative lives in application or request custody. Insert and Withdraw assets come from the configured application policy.

required-behavior.text: The following requirements describe intended protocol obligations. They have not been implemented or proved.

r1-registry-transitions-and-representati.text: Insert changes absent to Active and mints. Update changes Active to Over and burns. Delete changes Active to absent and burns. Over is terminal.

r2-native-request-construction.text: Application witnesses enforce creation. Singular validates consuming requests. An output at its address is not automatically admitted.

r3-insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: The configured policy approves the complete Insert proposal. Its correctness is an application obligation. Supported output parameters do not form a universal predicate language.

r4-insert-pending-completion-and-withdra.text: Insert waits without a representative. Folding requires absence. Cancellation requires a separate Withdraw asset bound to that exact pending request and refund effects.

r5-updatedelete-application-authorizatio.text: The application authorizes the selected operation and transfers its existing NFT to the exact request. No redundant attestation is required simply to repeat that release.

r6-updatedelete-custody-and-completion.text: A terminal request keeps its representative until completion. It cannot release it through ordinary withdrawal or sweep.

r7-folding-and-actor-permissions.text: Anyone may fold valid requests. The native logic has no mandatory arbitrary callback, but application asset disposal may invoke its policy. Fair inclusion is not guaranteed.

r8-replay-and-reincarnation.text: Spent requests cannot be spent again. Approval reuse must remain within its certified scope, including after a key is deleted and registered again.

r9-executing-witnesses-and-net-minting.text: Every obligation needs an executing witness. Logical mint and burn may net to zero, so policy invocation alone cannot be assumed to enforce all transitions.

acceptance-scenarios.text: These rejection and success cases are specification obligations, not executed tests. They cover approved requests, counterfeit authorization, custody escapes, replay and actual ledger witness boundaries.

illustrative-naming-demo-obligations.text: The proposed demo registers a name, resolves its authenticated address and changes that address locally. Naming and authorization details remain application choices.

open-decisions.text: Construction still needs encoding, policy binding, disposal, refunds, reincarnation, witness placement, batch limits and a naming profile.
